findings.title: Blocked address lookup is case-sensitive and can be trivially bypassed
findings.body: `should_block?` performs an exact database lookup using the raw submitted value. `User.new_from_params` also preserves the raw email, so a block for `user@example.com` does not match `user@EXAMPLE.COM` on the application's case-sensitive database, even though email domains are case-insensitive. An attacker can therefore evade an exact blocked-email rule simply by changing casing. Normalize emails consistently when storing and looking up blocked addresses (and enforce the same canonical form/index at the database level).

findings.title: Each blocked signup attempt increments match statistics twice
findings.body: The validator calls the mutating `BlockedEmail.should_block?` every time validations run. `UsersController#create` first calls `user.valid?` before the Discourse Hub check and then calls `user.save`, which validates again even when the first validation failed. Consequently one blocked registration request increments `match_count` twice and records two matches, so the statistics no longer represent blocked signup attempts. Move statistics recording out of validation or ensure it is performed only once per request.

findings.title: Blocked-email match counter updates are not atomic
findings.body: The counter is updated through a read-modify-write sequence on an ordinary Active Record instance. Concurrent validations of the same blocked address can both read the same `match_count` and save the same incremented value, losing matches; a delayed save can also overwrite a newer `last_match_at` with an older timestamp. Use an atomic SQL update/increment (or locking) to preserve the statistics under concurrent signup traffic.

findings.title: Rejected-email additions do not invalidate email validation
findings.body: `rejectedEmails` is an array of string values, but the computed property depends on `rejectedEmails.@each`. `@each` observes properties of array elements, not membership changes; pushing a rejected string at line 275 therefore does not invalidate the cached `emailValidation`. After the server rejects a blocked email, the UI can retain its previous successful validation and re-enable submission instead of showing the email as invalid. Depend on `rejectedEmails.[]` and add a client test covering the post-rejection state.
